prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a couple quick questions so I give the most useful recommendation:

- Do you mean Kansas City, Kansas (KS) or Kansas City, Missouri (MO)?  
- What type of coverage do you need: individual/family (ACA), Medicare, Medicaid, or small‑group/employer coverage?  
- Do you want an independent broker who will quote multiple carriers, or are you open to working with a captive agent (one carrier)?

If you want me to look up specific brokers in your area, give your ZIP code and the coverage type and I’ll produce a short list of licensed local brokers and contact details.

How to pick the best broker (short checklist)
- License & credentials: verify they are licensed in KS or MO with the state insurance department.  
- Specialty: make sure they have experience with the kind of plan you need (ACA marketplace vs. Medicare Advantage/Part D vs. employer plans).  
- Independence: independent brokers will compare multiple carriers; captive agents represent one carrier. Decide which you prefer.  
- Transparency on fees/commissions: ask how they’re paid and whether you’ll be charged directly.  
- Carrier access: confirm they can quote the major carriers available in your area.  
- References & reviews: check Google, Yelp, BBB, and ask for client references.  
- Availability & service: ask how they handle claims and ongoing plan changes (renewals, appeals).  

Useful resources to find and verify brokers
- Kansas Insurance Department and Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — license lookup and consumer complaint history.  
- Healthcare.gov (if you’re enrolling through the federal marketplace) or your state marketplace resources for in‑person assister lists.  
- NAHU (National Association of Health Underwriters) “Find an Agent” tool and local NAHU/NAIFA chapters for reputable agents.  
- Better Business Bureau and online reviews for reputation.

Questions to ask a broker during a call
- Which carriers and plans do you typically work with in my ZIP code?  
- Do you specialize in ACA plans, Medicare, or employer plans?  
- How do you get paid? Any costs to me?  
- Can you show me multiple plan options and walk through premiums, networks, deductibles, and out‑of‑pocket maximums?  
- Will you help with claims/appeals and plan changes after enrollment?  
- Can you provide references from clients with similar needs?

If you tell me your ZIP code and the kind of coverage you need, I’ll pull a short list of 3–5 licensed brokers in Kansas City with phone/email, specialties, and a quick sense of reputation so you can contact them.
